content: 1. Flemming K, Booth A, Hannes K, Cargo M, and Noyes J authored a paper as part of the Cochrane Qualitative and Implementation Methods Group guidance series. This paper, titled Paper 6: Reporting Guidelines for Qualitative, Implementation, and Process Evaluation Evidence Syntheses, provides detailed recommendations for reporting qualitative evidence synthesis findings. It was published in the Journal of Clinical Epidemiology and accessed on June 18, 2020. 2. Lewin S, Booth A, Glenton C, Munthe-Kaas H, Rashidian A, and Wainwright W, among others, introduced the application of GRADE-CERQual to qualitative evidence synthesis findings. This work, titled Applying GRADE-CERQual to Qualitative Evidence Synthesis Findings: Introduction to the Series, was published in Implementation Science in 2018 and accessed on June 18, 2020. 3. Booth A, Lewin S, Glenton C, Munthe-Kaas H, Toews I, and Jane Noyes, among others, explored the potential impacts of dissemination bias in qualitative evidence synthesis. Their work, Paper 7: Understanding the Potential Impacts of Dissemination Bias, was published in Implementation Science in 2018 and accessed on June 18, 2020. 4. Downie S, Finlayson KW, Lawrie TA, Lewin SA, Glenton C, and Rosenbaum S, among others, authored a series of papers on the use of qualitative evidence synthesis (QES) in developing clinical and health systems guidelines. The first paper, Using Qualitative Evidence Synthesis to Inform Guideline Scope and Develop Qualitative Findings Statements, was published in Health Research Policy and Systems in 2019. 5. Lewin S, Glenton C, Lawrie TA, Downie S, Finlayson KW, and Rosenbaum S, among others, contributed to the second paper in the series, Using Qualitative Evidence Synthesis Findings to Inform Evidence-to-Decision Frameworks and Recommendations, published in Health Research Policy and Systems in 2019. 6. Glenton C, Lewin S, Lawrie TA, Barreix M, Downie S, and Finlayson KW, among others, authored the third paper in the series, Using Qualitative Evidence Syntheses to Develop Implementation Considerations and Inform Implementation Processes, published in Health Research Policy and Systems in 2019. 7. Langlois EV, Daniels K, and Akl EA edited a comprehensive methods guide titled Evidence Synthesis for Health Policy and Systems, published by the World Health Organization in 2018. This guide provides a detailed framework for conducting evidence synthesis to inform health policy and systems decision-making. 8. Lockwood C, Porritt K, Munn Z, Rittenmeyer L, Salmond S, and Bjerrum M, among others, contributed to Chapter 2 of the Joanna Briggs Institute Reviewer’s Manual. This chapter, Systematic Reviews of Qualitative Evidence, outlines the methodology for conducting systematic reviews of qualitative research. 9. Pearson A, Robertson-Malt S, and Rittenmeyer L authored a guide titled Synthesizing Qualitative Evidence: The Joanna Briggs Institute, which provides practical guidance for synthesizing qualitative research findings. 10. The Swedish Agency for Health Technology Assessment and Assessment of Social Services (SBU) published a document titled Evaluation and Synthesis of Studies Using Qualitative Methods of Analysis, which provides methodological guidance for qualitative evidence synthesis. 11. Noyes J and Lewin S authored Chapter 5 of the Cochrane Collaboration’s supplementary guidance for including qualitative research in systematic reviews of interventions. This chapter, Extracting Qualitative Evidence, provides detailed instructions for data extraction in qualitative evidence synthesis. 12. The GRADE-CERQual approach, developed by Lewin S, Glenton C, Munthe-Kaas H, Carlsen B, Colvin CJ, and Gülmezoglu M, among others, provides a framework for assessing confidence in findings from qualitative evidence syntheses. This approach was detailed in a 2015 publication in PLOS Medicine. 13. Butler A, Hall H, and Copnell B authored a guide titled A Guide to Writing a Qualitative Systematic Review Protocol to Enhance Evidence-Based Practice in Nursing and Healthcare, published in Worldviews on Evidence-Based Nursing in 2016. 14. Booth A, Noyes J, Flemming K, Moore G, Tunçalp Ö, and Shakibazadeh E developed a framework for formulating questions to explore complex interventions within qualitative evidence synthesis. This framework was published in BMJ Global Health. 15. Cooke A, Smith D, and Booth A introduced the SPIDER tool for qualitative evidence synthesis in their 2012 publication in Qualitative Health Research. This tool provides a structured approach to identifying and synthesizing qualitative research. 16. Munabi-Babigumira S, Glenton C, Lewin S, Fretheim A, and Nabudere H conducted a qualitative evidence synthesis on factors influencing the provision of intrapartum and postnatal care by skilled birth attendants in lowand middle-income countries. This synthesis was published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2017. 17. Harris JL, Booth A, Cargo M, Hannes K, Harden A, and Flemming K, among others, authored Paper 2: Methods for Question Formulation, Searching, and Protocol Development for Qualitative Evidence Synthesis, published in the Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2018. 18. Booth A authored a methodological review titled Searching for Qualitative Research for Inclusion in Systematic Reviews, published in Systematic Reviews in 2016. This review provides a structured approach to identifying qualitative research. 19. Glenton C, Colvin CJ, Carlsen B, Swartz A, Lewin S, and Noyes J, among others, explored barriers and facilitators to implementing lay health worker programs in their qualitative evidence synthesis.
